reader.requirement: At --std 85, FUNCTION LOG10 of a class-numeric argument greater than zero returns a numeric approximation of its base-10 logarithm. The argument can have any usage or scale, or be a literal or an arithmetic expression. The precision and other characteristics of the result are implementor-defined.

edition-consulted.switches: D8 window: sig.IntroducedIn (85 on the catalog row) > ctx.Edition.DialectLevel raises COBOL1502, RemovedIn raises the removal error; at --std 85 neither fires

ConstructRegistry numeric-function-identifier-operand-2002: below 2002 a numeric/integer function written where an identifier stands (MOVE, DISPLAY) is refused COBOL0900; a function inside an arithmetic expression is not screened

the OPTIONS paragraph (so ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-*) is refused below 2002, so NumericRenderer#StandardDecimal is false at 85 and the renderer takes its native arm, the same arm 2023 takes with no OPTIONS paragraph

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel/Edition/CobolVersion/ConstructRegistry over IntrinsicRenderer.cs and src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Intrinsics: no hits. The only switch on the value path is num.StandardDecimal (the ARITHMETIC mode), which 85 cannot reach.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the returned value: log1.cob prints the same output at --std 85 and 2023. Use as an identifier operand is refused only at 85, and that is outside this rule.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers one ill-conditioned argument near 1. Exact powers of ten, fractions, the 18-digit extremes, table elements and COMP-3 arguments are not exercised.

probes.expected: approximation of log10 of the exact argument

probes.printed: COBOL0900: numeric function-identifier (LOG10) where an identifier is written requires COBOL-2002
COBOL1627: LOG argument-1 is of class alphanumeric

probes.expected: at 85 the result is undefined (§1989:A.2.2, AR2: a value outside the permissible range), so any value conforms

citations.check: OK  §1989:A.2.21.4 RV1  (2.21.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV1 ['approximation of the logarithm to the base 10 of argument-1']

OK  §1989:A.2.3  (2.3 TYPES OF FUNCTIONS)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GR2 ['Those characteristics of the returned value not otherwise specified for a given function are defined by the implementor']
OK  §1989:A.2.21.3 AR2  (2.21.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR2 ['The value of argument-1 must be greater than zero']

reader.notes: LOG10 runs through a binary64 body, with an exact (wide) intake near the ill-conditioned point. Results carry about 16 significant digits: ln(999999999999999999) prints 41.446531673892820, where the exact value is 41.446531673892822... §1989:A.2.3 leaves that precision of the 'approximation' to the implementor. The value path consults no edition.
reader.at-2023: log1.cob prints the same output at --std 2023

location-remarks.src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Intri: LOG10 row: Numeric, Float, Domain Positive, IntroducedIn 85

LOG10 as a user data-name with FUNCTION LOG10(LOG10) = 1 (FNW.cob). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.21.4 RV1 'approximation of the logarithm to the base 10'; OK §1989:A.2.3 (GR2) on implementor-defined characteristics.
